source: TSTD project (TA 7305-CAM), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំពោត" (Corn Cultivation Technical Manual), Section 4.a: Diseases and prevention, May 2012
text:
The manual describes three corn diseases and their prevention/control methods:

1) Leaf blight (ជម្ងឺផុះលៀងស្លឹក): Symptoms are yellowing leaf tips, spreading from one plant to the next in the row with a dry, water-soaked appearance; if left untreated the disease spreads through the field. Prevention: use disease-resistant varieties; cut off and remove diseased plants, then burn or bury them far from the field; spray a registered fungicide such as metalaxyl or another fungicide proven effective against this disease, following label instructions.

2) Pythium stalk rot (ជម្ងឺល្អយដើម / Phythium Stalk Rot): Symptoms are a soft, blackened, rotten stem base with a slimy/mucus coating, and leaves that wilt and droop when touched. Prevention: ensure good field drainage to avoid waterlogging; cut and remove diseased plants, burning or burying them away from the field; spray a registered fungicide such as metalaxyl, or another fungicide proven effective against this disease, following label instructions.

3) Banded leaf and sheath blight (ជម្ងឺរលាកដំបៅដើម / Banded Leaf & Sheath Blight): Symptoms are dry brownish patches on the leaf sheath that start on the lower/older leaves and progress upward; the disease spreads quickly under high humidity, particularly in densely planted fields. Prevention: use disease-resistant varieties; cut off and remove affected leaves/sheaths and burn or bury them away from the field; spray as soon as symptoms are seen to stop it spreading, using a registered fungicide proven effective against this disease, following label instructions.
